answer: My pick is SRAM PUF challenge-response. Each operator buys a $15 board whose memory powers up in a noise pattern unique to that one chip. At enrollment the verifier records 200 challenge-response pairs and keeps them secret. Every epoch the ledger sends one unused challenge; the board must reply within 4 seconds, and a match unlocks that epoch's attestation. Faking 1,000 agents means 1,000 boards, about $15,000 plus $3,000 shipping, because one chip can't spiral into many identities. It works like ivory grain or the glow of an ember: no two pieces ever burn the same.
